title: OpenAI Wants Every AI Lab to Cap Perplexity for Safety
dek: Chief scientist Jakub Pachocki shares OpenAI's internal scores and asks rivals to join.
caption:
OpenAI just handed its rivals a look at its own internal scorecard, and it's asking them to do the same. 👀

Chief scientist Jakub Pachocki proposes a shared AI safety standard built on one number: perplexity, a measure of how well a model predicts unseen text. Labs would report it openly, agree on testing and red-teaming norms, and commit to common limits that stay in place until safety tools, like successors to chain-of-thought monitors, catch up.

The published numbers show GPT-3.5 at about 0.99, GPT-4 at about 0.91, and recent models below 0.8, with major gains in cybersecurity and math. Pachocki warns AI helping build AI could trigger a sudden jump as soon as 2027, and that alignment audits may weaken as models get smarter.

It's only a proposal, and comparing scores across labs won't be easy. We're following whether Anthropic, Google and others sign on here at AI Parabellum.
